questions.q: In a digital control system, which block converts the controller output back into an analog signal?
questions.explain: The DAC (with its hold) turns the controller's numbers into a continuous signal for the plant.

questions.q: Which is a disadvantage of digital control?
options: Computational delay and a limit set by the sampling frequency
questions.explain: Digital control is cheap and flexible, but it needs an ADC and a DAC, is limited by the sampling rate, and the computation adds delay.

questions.q: The three processes inside an ADC, in order, are
questions.explain: Sample in time, round the amplitude to a level, then write the level as a binary code.

questions.q: $x(t) = \sin(200\pi t)$ is sampled every 1 ms. What is the signal frequency?
questions.explain: $\omega = 200\pi = 2\pi f$, so $f = 100$ Hz; $f_s = 1000$ Hz satisfies Nyquist (≥ 200 Hz).

questions.q: A signal has components up to 1.2 kHz and is sampled at 1.5 kHz. At what frequency does the 1.2 kHz component appear?
questions.explain: It is above the 750 Hz Nyquist frequency, so it folds to $|1200 - 1500| = 300$ Hz.

questions.q: The Nyquist rate of a signal whose highest frequency is $f_{max}$ is
questions.explain: Perfect reconstruction needs $f_s \ge 2f_{max}$; $2f_{max}$ is the Nyquist rate.

questions.q: A rule of thumb for a control loop with closed-loop bandwidth 80 Hz is to sample at about
questions.explain: Use 5–10× the bandwidth (at least 10× for good control), with an anti-aliasing filter.

questions.q: What prevents aliasing?
options: An analog low-pass filter before the ADC, and a high enough sampling rate
A digital filter after the ADC
questions.explain: Once aliased, the samples are identical to the false signal; the high frequencies must be removed before sampling.

questions.q: A 3-bit ADC covers 0–8 V. What is the step size $\Delta$?
What is the resolution of a 12-bit ADC, in percent?
The maximum quantisation error of a rounding quantiser with step $\Delta$ is
questions.explain: Each input is rounded to the nearest level, so it is never more than half a step away.

questions.q: $\mathcal{Z}\{\delta(k - 3)\}$ is
questions.explain: A single unit sample at $k = 3$ gives the single term $z^{-3}$.

questions.q: The ROC of the unit step $z/(z - 1)$ is
questions.explain: The series $1 + z^{-1} + \cdots$ converges for $|z^{-1}| < 1$, i.e. outside the unit circle.

questions.q: $\mathcal{Z}\{a^k\}$ for $k \ge 0$ is
questions.explain: Geometric series: $\sum(az^{-1})^k = 1/(1 - az^{-1}) = z/(z - a)$, for $|z| > |a|$.

questions.q: The z-transform of a sampled unit ramp $f(kT) = kT$ is
questions.explain: From $zF - F = Tz/(z - 1)$.

questions.q: The final-value theorem in the z-domain is
questions.explain: Valid only if $(z - 1)X(z)$ has all its poles inside the unit circle; $\lim_{z\to\infty}X(z)$ is the initial value.

questions.q: Shifting a sequence one place to the right (a delay) multiplies its transform by
questions.explain: $\mathcal{Z}\{r(k - 1)\} = z^{-1}R(z)$; $z^{-1}$ is the unit delay.

questions.q: The difference equation $y(k) = 0.5y(k - 1) + x(k)$ has transfer function
By long division, $E(z) = \dfrac{23z^3 + 13z^2 - 15z}{z^3 - z^2 + z + 3}$ gives $e(1) =$ ?
For $X(z) = \dfrac{z^2}{(z - 1)(z - 0.5)}$, what is $x(2)$?
Why is the partial-fraction expansion done on $X(z)/z$?
options: Because the table pairs have $z$ in the numerator, e.g. $z/(z - a) \leftrightarrow a^k$
questions.explain: Expanding $X(z)/z$ and multiplying back by $z$ gives terms of the form $Az/(z - a)$.

questions.q: The transfer function of a zero-order hold is
questions.explain: Its impulse response is one pulse of height 1 and width $T$: a step minus a delayed step.

questions.q: On average, a ZOH delays the signal by about
questions.explain: The staircase lags the samples by half a period, which reduces the phase margin.

questions.q: The ZOH equivalent of $1/(s + 2)$ with $T = 0.5$ s is $b/(z - 0.368)$. Find $b$.
The ZOH equivalent of $1/(s + a)$ is
questions.explain: The $1/a$ is needed so that the DC gain $G(1) = 1/a$ matches the plant; the slides omit it.

questions.q: Which discretisation maps the whole $j\omega$ axis onto the unit circle (no aliasing, but frequency warping)?
questions.explain: Tustin squeezes $0 \le \omega < \infty$ onto the circle, so frequencies are warped but never aliased.

questions.q: Two blocks $G_1(s)$ and $G_2(s)$ are in cascade with **no** sampler between them. The pulse transfer function is
questions.explain: Blocks in one continuous path must be multiplied in $s$ before transforming.

questions.q: A loop has a sampler in the forward path only, with $G(s)$ forward and $H(s)$ in the feedback. $C(z)/R(z) =$
questions.explain: $G$ and $H$ are in one continuous path round the loop, so the loop term is $GH(z)$.

questions.q: Unity feedback round $G(z) = z/(z - 0.8)$ gives
A discrete LTI system is stable if all its poles satisfy
questions.explain: $z = e^{sT}$ maps the left half-plane inside the unit circle.

questions.q: Repeated poles on the unit circle make a system
questions.explain: A double pole at $z = 1$, for example, gives a response that grows linearly.

questions.q: The poles of $z^2 + 1.2z + 0.32$ are
questions.explain: $(z + 0.4)(z + 0.8)$; both inside the circle, so stable. The notes give +0.4 and +0.8.

questions.q: A controller has poles at 0.6 and 1.05. It is
questions.explain: 1.05 is outside the unit circle; that mode grows as $1.05^k$.

questions.q: The bilinear substitution used for the stability test is
questions.explain: Its inverse is $s = (z + 1)/(z - 1)$; it maps $|z| < 1$ onto $\text{Re}(s) < 0$. The notes once misprint $s - 2$.

questions.q: Substituting the bilinear map into $z^2 - z + 0.2$ gives
questions.explain: All coefficients positive, so stable; the z-roots are 0.724 and 0.276.

questions.q: Second-order Jury conditions for $a_2z^2 + a_1z + a_0$ ($a_2 > 0$) are
questions.explain: These three conditions put both roots inside the unit circle.

questions.q: Unity feedback with $G(z) = K/[(z - 1)(z - 0.5)]$. What is the largest $K$ for stability?
questions.explain: Characteristic equation $z^2 - 1.5z + 0.5 + K$; $|0.5 + K| < 1$ gives $K < 0.5$.

questions.q: Making the sampling period larger in a loop with a stable analog plant
options: Can push the z-poles outside the unit circle
questions.explain: For $K/[s(s + 1)]$ with a ZOH, the largest stable $K$ falls from 20.3 at $T = 0.1$ s to 1.46 at $T = 2$ s.

questions.q: A digital lag compensator $K(z - z_0)/(z - p_0)$ has
questions.explain: Its pole is nearer $z = 1$, giving a DC gain $(1 - z_0)/(1 - p_0) > 1$. The slides have the inequalities for lag and lead swapped.

questions.q: The main purpose of a lead compensator is to
options: Improve the transient response and the phase margin
questions.explain: A lead gives a faster rise and less overshoot; a lag improves accuracy.

questions.q: In the velocity-form PID, the derivative term is
questions.explain: Differencing the position-form derivative once more gives the second backward difference.

questions.q: Velocity PID with $K_p = 1$, $K_i = 2$, $K_d = 0.05$, $T = 0.1$ and all past values zero: $e[0] = 1$. Find $u[0]$.
Unity feedback with $K(z + 0.5)/[z(z - 0.8)]$. The loop is stable for $0 < K <$ ?
questions.explain: Characteristic equation $z^2 + (K - 0.8)z + 0.5K$; $0.5K < 1$. At $K = 2$ the poles are $-0.6 \pm j0.8$.

questions.q: For MIMO state feedback $u[k] = -Kx[k]$, the design goal is
options: the eigenvalues of $A - BK$ inside the unit circle
the eigenvalues of $A$ on the unit circle
questions.explain: The closed loop is $x[k + 1] = (A - BK)x[k]$.

questions.q: In the RC lead network $\beta\dfrac{1 + \tau s}{1 + \beta\tau s}$, $\beta$ is
questions.explain: $\beta = R_2/(R_1 + R_2) < 1$, so the zero ($-1/\tau$) is nearer the origin than the pole.

questions.q: A design needs $\zeta = 0.6$. What percentage overshoot does the dominant pair give?
Why can a PI controller not supply 57.6° of phase lead in the PD example?
questions.explain: The design formula then gives a negative $K_i$, which is meaningless; PD or lead is needed.

questions.q: For $A = \begin{bmatrix}0 & 1\\-2 & -3\end{bmatrix}$, $B = [0\;\;5]^T$, $C = [1\;\;0]$, the transfer function is
questions.explain: $\det(sI - A) = s^2 + 3s + 2$; the summary's $s(s - 3) + 2$ is a sign error.

questions.q: A sampled state model $x[k + 1] = \Phi x[k] + \Gamma u[k]$ has $\Phi =$
questions.explain: Each eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $A$ becomes $e^{\lambda T}$, the same $z = e^{sT}$ mapping.

questions.q: For $G(z) = \dfrac{K(z + 1)}{(z - 1)(z - 0.5)}$ in unity feedback, the range of $K$ for stability is
questions.explain: Jury: $D(1) = 2K > 0$ and $|K + 0.5| < 1$. At $K = 0.5$ the poles are $0.5 \pm j0.866$, on the unit circle. ($K = 1.5$ is where the locus crosses the imaginary axis, which is not a boundary in the z-plane.)

questions.q: In the z-plane, the root-locus gain at the stability limit is found where the locus crosses
questions.explain: Stability needs $|z| < 1$, so the limit is where a branch reaches the unit circle.

questions.q: A design needs $\zeta = 0.5$ and $\omega_n = 4$ rad/s with $T = 0.2$ s. What is $|z|$ of the desired closed-loop pole?
questions.explain: $|z| = e^{-\zeta\omega_nT} = e^{-0.4} = 0.6703$; its angle is $\omega_dT = 3.464 \times 0.2 = 39.7°$.

questions.q: A digital lead controller $K\dfrac{z - 0.6703}{z - p}$ is chosen with its zero at the plant pole 0.6703 mainly to
questions.explain: Cancelling a slow pole simplifies the locus; the controller pole is then placed to meet the angle condition.

questions.q: ZOH and $\dfrac{10}{s(s + 1)}$ in a stable unity-feedback loop. What is the steady-state error for a unit ramp?
The type of a digital loop is the number of open-loop poles at
questions.explain: A pole at $z = 1$ is a digital integrator, the counterpart of $s = 0$.

questions.q: ZOH and $\dfrac{20}{s + 5}$ in unity feedback. What is the largest sampling period (s) for stability?
questions.explain: The closed-loop pole is $5e^{-5T} - 4$; $|z| < 1$ gives $T < \frac15\ln\frac53 = 0.102$ s.

questions.q: ZOH and $\dfrac{1}{s(s + 1)}$ with unit gain in unity feedback. Up to what sampling period (s) is the loop stable?
questions.explain: The characteristic equation is $z^2 + (T - 2)z + 1 - Te^{-T} = 0$; $D(-1) > 0$ needs $T(1 + e^{-T}) < 4$, so $T < 3.92$ s.

questions.q: After the bilinear transformation, the Routh table of $D(s)$ has one sign change in its first column. The z-plane system has
options: One pole outside the unit circle
One pole on the unit circle
One pole inside the unit circle
One zero outside the unit circle
questions.explain: Each sign change is a right-half-plane root of $D(s)$, which is a pole outside the unit circle.

questions.q: A deadbeat controller places the closed-loop poles at
questions.explain: All poles at the origin make the response settle in a finite number of samples, at the cost of large control effort.

questions.q: The main practical advantage of model predictive control is that it
options: Handles input and output constraints explicitly
questions.explain: MPC optimises over a receding horizon and can include limits on inputs and outputs.

questions.q: The sampled double integrator is measured through velocity only, $C = [0\;\;1]$. It is
questions.explain: $M_c$ has full rank, but $M_o = \begin{bmatrix}0 & 1\\0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$ is singular: position cannot be recovered from velocity.

questions.q: How many roots of $z^3 - 2.2z^2 + 1.21z + 0.338$ lie outside the unit circle?
questions.explain: It factors as $(z + 0.2)(z^2 - 2.4z + 1.69)$; the pair $1.2 \pm j0.5$ has $|z| = 1.3$.
